name: Pelham Bay Bridge
facts: Pelham Bay Bridge, completed in 1907 by the New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad, originally featured three parallel two‑track spans, a testament to early 20th‑century rail engineering in the Bronx.
Amtrak’s 2009 rehabilitation of Pelham Bay Bridge capped a century of service, yet the structure remains obsolete, limiting train speeds to 45 miles per hour and demanding constant maintenance.
In 2019, Amtrak and the MTA agreed that the MTA would fund a new high‑level fixed bridge, enabling future Penn Station Access trains to use the historic Pelham Bay Bridge route.
